methods.name: Peer-Median

data.narrative:
Kraftblock is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Martin Schichtel and Susanne König, having raised €20M+ to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comparable universe of nine private and one public peer (LNZA), including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Redwood Materials, and QuantumScape, predominantly at Series C stage within the Climate & Energy sector.

Two triangulation methods apply to this stage and data availability. Stage-progression analysis, using the €20M+ total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yields €38M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C)—produces a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range of $700M–$3.0B. The significant dispersion reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity and capital intensity across climate-tech.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $32M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $519M. The stage-progression method produces a conservative floor, while peer comparables anchor the upper range. Key uncertainties include Kraftblock's specific technology readiness level, path to commercialization, and capital requirements relative to peers—factors that would materially influence placement within this range.
